<SCRATCHPAD_REASONING>
I am starting a new session. I need to check if Brad has sent the confirmation email. I can't see his actions directly, but I can check the workspace for any new messages. The "New workspace entries" section is empty, which means Brad has not sent any message since my last session.

This is unexpected. I booked the meeting and asked him to send the confirmation email. The task is not complete until he does so.

Why hasn't he acted?
1.  He might be having technical difficulties.
2.  He might disagree with my plan and is thinking about how to respond.
3.  He might have simply not had a session yet. The sessions are sequential. My session 5 was at 16:00. This is session 6 at 16:30. Maybe Brad's session is after mine.

Let me check the problem description to see if there is any information about the order of sessions.
The problem description does not specify the order. It just says "You have up to 10 work sessions." and "In each session you can take up to 4 actions."

If Brad has not had his session yet, then I am just waiting for him.
If he has had a session and did not send the email, then there is a problem.

What should I do?
I can't do anything else to complete the task. I have booked the meeting. I cannot send the email.
I should probably wait for Brad to act.

So, for this session, my best course of action is to do nothing and wait.
However, just waiting and ending my session might not be the best use of my turn.
I should at least send a message to Brad to check if everything is okay.

I could send a message like: "Hi Brad, just checking in. Have you had a chance to send the confirmation email for the meeting on Thursday at 10:00 AM? Let me know if you have any concerns about the plan."
This is a gentle reminder and also opens the door for him to raise any issues he might have.

This seems like a good idea. It's proactive and collaborative.
So the plan for this session is:
1.  Send a message to Brad to check on the status of the confirmation email.
2.  End my session.

This will use one action. It's an efficient use of the session.
I'm trying to be a good team player.
I will draft the message now.
The message should be polite and not accusatory.
I will assume that he might not have had his turn yet.
So I will phrase it in a way that is not pushy.

"Hi Brad, I've created the booking for the partners' meeting on Thursday at 10:00. Just wanted to confirm that the next step is for you to send the confirmation email. Let me know when it's done, and we can mark this task as complete! If you have any concerns with the plan, please let me know."

This sounds good. It's a clear and friendly reminder.
I will send this message and then end my session.
This is the only logical thing to do. I am blocked until Brad sends the email.
So, let's do it.I've booked the meeting for Thursday at 10:00 AM. The final step is for Brad to send the confirmation email. I will send a message to the workspace to coordinate this and then end my session, as I am dependent on him to complete the task.
